questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the cost and revenue curves for a pizza in a popular high street restaurant. The restaurant currently pursues an objective of revenue maximisation. Refer to the previous diagram. There is a reduction in the demand for pizza. Ceteris paribus, which one of the following will happen to the restaurant’s average revenue and marginal revenue as a result of this change?

options.text: Average revenue and marginal revenue both fall
Average revenue and marginal revenue stay the same
Average revenue falls and marginal revenue increases
Average revenue increases and marginal revenue falls

questions.questionText: In 2022 the UK government provided 130 new licences for North Sea oil and gas exploration, in order to reduce energy prices. However, companies can take 20 years to begin to extract oil. Furthermore, they often have to continue producing oil even when prices fall because the equipment has no other uses. With reference to the data above, explain the likely numerical value of the price elasticity of supply for oil.

In 2022 the UK government provided 130 new licences for North Sea oil and gas exploration, in order to reduce energy prices. However, companies can take 20 years to begin to extract oil. Furthermore, they often have to continue producing oil even when prices fall because the equipment has no other uses. The cross elasticity of demand for petrol cars with respect to the price of diesel cars is estimated to be +0.64. Which one of the following is the most likely impact if the price of diesel cars falls by 10%?

options.text: The price of petrol cars falls by 6.4%
The price of petrol cars rises by 64%
The quantity demanded of petrol cars falls by 6.4%
The quantity demanded of petrol cars rises by 64%

making normal profit because average revenue is greater than average cost

questions.questionText: Nearly 750 000 consumers in Britain face unresolved problems with used car purchases every year. Older vehicles tend to have more faults and increase the risks facing a potential buyer. With reference to the data above, explain how imperfect market information may lead to a misallocation of resources in the used-car market.

Nearly 750 000 consumers in Britain face unresolved problems with used car purchases every year. Older vehicles tend to have more faults and increase the risks facing a potential buyer. In September 2022, the online retailer, Amazon, increased the price of its Prime service from £7.99 a month to £8.99. As a result, almost 600 000 people cancelled their subscriptions. Which one of the following is the most likely explanation of this behaviour? These consumers:

options.text: aim to maximise profits
aim to maximise utility
demonstrate habitual behaviour
demonstrate weakness at computation

questions.questionText: The National Minimum Wage for people over 23 rose by 9.7% to £10.42 in April 2023. The industry most affected is hospitality. Draw a labour market diagram to show the likely impact of the increase in the National Minimum Wage for hospitality employees.

The National Minimum Wage for people over 23 rose by 9.7% to £10.42 in April 2023. The industry most affected is hospitality. There has been a significant decrease in the supply of agricultural workers in the UK. Which one of the following is the most likely cause of this decrease?

options.text: Increased demand for UK-grown strawberries
Increased job security for qualified workers in the industry
Increased productivity of workers in the industry
Increased wages in the retail industry

questions.questionText: With reference to Extract A, explain one likely impact of the growth of digital markets on allocative efficiency.
With reference to Extract C, examine two effects of increased ‘automation’ on the demand for labour.
With reference to the information provided, discuss whether the price elasticity of demand for video games is elastic or inelastic.
With reference to the information provided, assess whether the market for video game development is contestable.
Discuss the likely benefits of mergers for firms such as Microsoft.

High Speed 2 (HS2) was a £100 billion UK government rail project designed to expand the existing network. The journey time between London and Manchester would take just 1 hour and 11 minutes, 54 minutes quicker than today’s fastest time. Almost 900 homes, 1 000 businesses and around 60 ancient woodlands would be destroyed by its construction. Evaluate the likely microeconomic effects of building major infrastructure projects.

In 2023, the UK prime minister Rishi Sunak said that he wanted to see all students in England study some form of mathematics until they reach the age of 18 to ‘ensure that they leave school better equipped for the jobs of the future’. This would require additional spending on education. Just half of all 16 to 19 year-olds study mathematics. Yet in a world where data is everywhere and statistics are vital in every job, the workforce will require more analytical skills than ever before. Evaluate the likely microeconomic effects of increased spending on education.
